title.zh: 卷八十五 晉書11: 少帝本紀五
title.en: Volume 85 Book of Later Jin 11: Emperor Shao 4
title.raw: 卷八十五 晉書11: 少帝本紀五 Volume 85 Book of Later Jin 11: Emperor Shao 4

sentences.zh: 開運三年冬十月甲子，正衙命使冊皇太妃安氏。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter of the third year of Kaiyun, on the day jiazi, an envoy appointed at the main audience hall enfeoffed Grand Imperial Consort Lady An.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day in the tenth month of winter, Kaiyun year 3, an envoy commissioned at the main court invested Lady An as Grand Imperial Consort.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以樞密直學士、禮部侍郎邊光範為翰林學士，以給事中邊歸讜為左散騎常侍，以翰林學士、祠部員外郎、知制誥張沆為右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: On jichou, Bian Guangfan, Direct Academician of the Palace Secretariat and Vice Minister of Rites, was made Hanlin Academician; Bian Guichan, Supervising Secretary, was made Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse; Zhang Hong, Hanlin Academician, Clerk of the Ministry of Rites (extra rank), and Drafter of Imperial Edicts, was made Right Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Bian Guangfan—Direct Academician of the Palace Secretariat and Vice Minister of Rites—was appointed Hanlin Academician; Bian Guichan, Supervising Secretary, became Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse; and Zhang Hong, Hanlin Academician, Clerk of the Ministry of Rites (extra rank), and Drafter of Imperial Edicts, was made Right Remonstrating Censor.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以鄴都留守杜威為北面行營都招討使，以侍衛親軍都指揮使、鄆州節度使李守貞為兵馬都監，兗州安審琦為左右廂都指揮使，徐州符彥卿為馬軍左廂都指揮使，滑州皇甫遇為馬軍右廂都指揮使，貝州梁漢璋為馬軍都排陣使，前鄧州宋彥筠為步軍左廂都指揮使，奉國左廂都指揮使王饒為步軍右廂都指揮使，洺州團練使薛懷讓為先鋒都指揮使。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Du Wei, Military Governor of Ye, was made Grand Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Campaign Headquarters; Li Shouzhen, Commander-in-Chief of the Imperial Guard and Military Governor of Yanzhou, was made Overall Supervisor of Troops and Horses; An Shenqi of Yanzhou was made Commander of the Left and Right Wings; Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou was made Commander of the Left Wing of the Horse Army; Huangfu Yu of Huazhou was made Commander of the Right Wing of the Horse Army; Liang Hanzhang of Beizhou was made Marshal of the Horse Army Array; Song Yanjun, former Military Governor of Dengzhou, was made Commander of the Left Wing of the Foot Army; Wang Rao, Commander of the Left Wing of the Fengguo Army, was made Commander of the Right Wing of the Foot Army; Xue Huairang, Militia Commissioner of Mingzhou, was made Vanguard Commander.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Du Wei, who held Ye as his base, was appointed overall commander of the northern campaign; Li Shouzhen, commander of the imperial guard and military governor of Yanzhou, became supervisor of all troops and horses; An Shenqi of Yanzhou took command of both wings; Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou headed the left wing of the cavalry; Huangfu Yu of Huazhou the right wing of the cavalry; Liang Hanzhang of Beizhou marshaled the cavalry formation; the former governor of Dengzhou, Song Yanjun, led the left wing of the infantry; Wang Rao, commander of the Fengguo left wing, the right wing of the infantry; and Xue Huairang, militia commissioner of Mingzhou, served as vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: （案：《通鑒》載，當時敕榜曰：「先取瀛、鄚，安定關南；

translations.literal: (Note: Zizhi Tongjian records that the edict placard of the time read: "First take Ying and Mo and secure the lands south of the pass;
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian: The edict placard of the time proclaimed, "First seize Ying and Mo and secure the territory south of the pass;

sentences.zh: 次復幽、燕，蕩平塞北。

translations.literal: then recover You and Yan and sweep the northern frontier clean."
translations.idiomatic: then recover You and Yan and pacify the entire northern frontier."

sentences.zh: 」蓋狃於陽城之役而驟驕也。）〉

translations.literal: This was because they clung to the victory at Yangcheng and suddenly grew arrogant.)]
translations.idiomatic: They had grown overconfident after Yangcheng and were suddenly boastful.)]

sentences.zh: 癸酉，冊吳國夫人馮氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Lady Feng, Lady of the State of Wu, was invested as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Lady Feng of Wu was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以侍衛馬軍都指揮使李彥韜權知侍衛司事。

translations.literal: On yihai, Li Yantao, Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Horse Army of the Imperial Guard, was appointed Acting Director of the Imperial Guard Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Li Yantao, commander of the imperial guard cavalry, was placed in temporary charge of the imperial guard bureau.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，鳳翔節度使秦王李從嚴薨，輟朝，冊贈尚書令。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Li Congyan, Prince of Qin and Military Governor of Fengxiang, died; court audiences were suspended, and posthumously he was enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Li Congyan, Prince of Qin and military governor of Fengxiang, died; the court suspended audiences and posthumously invested him as Grand Master of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，邠州節度使李德充卒，輟朝，贈太尉。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Li Dechong, Military Governor of Binzhou, died; court audiences were suspended, and he was posthumously given the title Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Li Dechong, military governor of Binzhou, died; audiences were suspended and he was posthumously made Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊子朔，以給事中盧撰為右散騎常侍，以尚書兵部郎中兼侍御史、知雜事陳觀為左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month, wuzi, Lu Zhuan, Supervising Secretary, was made Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse; Chen Guan, Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs in the Ministry of War and concurrent Censor and Chief of Miscellaneous Affairs, was made Left Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month, wuzi, Supervising Secretary Lu Zhuan became Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse, and Chen Guan, director in the Bureau of Military Affairs who also served as censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs, was appointed Left Remonstrating Censor.

sentences.zh: 觀以祖諱「義」，乞改官，尋授給事中。

translations.literal: Because Guan's grandfather's taboo name was "Yi," he requested a change of office and was soon appointed Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Because his grandfather's taboo name was Yi, Guan asked to be reassigned and was soon made Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，樞密使、中書侍郎兼戶部尚書、平章事馮玉加尚書右僕射，以皇子鎮寧軍節度使延煦為陜州節度使，以陜州留後焦繼勛為鳳翔留後，以前定州留後安審琦為邠州留後，以右僕射和凝為左僕射。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Feng Yu, Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, Vice Director of the Secretariat concurrent Minister of Revenue and Grand Councilor, was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; the prince Yanshu, Military Governor of Zhenning Army, was made Military Governor of Shanzhou; Jiao Jixun, Acting Governor of Shanzhou, was made Acting Governor of Fengxiang; An Shenqi, former Acting Governor of Dingzhou, was made Acting Governor of Binzhou; and He Ning, Right Vice Director, was made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Feng Yu, palace commissioner, vice director of the secretariat, concurrent minister of revenue, and grand councilor, was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Prince Yanshu, military governor of Zhenning, was sent to Shanzhou; Jiao Jixun, acting governor of Shanzhou, to Fengxiang; the former acting governor of Dingzhou, An Shenqi, to Binzhou; and He Ning moved from right to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 甲午，兩浙節度使吳越國王錢宏佐起復舊任。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Qian Hongzuo, King of Wuyue and Military Governor of the Two Zhes, resumed his former post after mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Qian Hongzuo, King of Wuyue and military governor of the Two Zhes, returned from mourning to his former duties.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔李守貞知幽州行府事。

translations.literal: On dingyou, an edict appointed Li Shouzhen to administer the mobile headquarters at Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Li Shouzhen was ordered to take charge of the campaign headquarters at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊申，日南至，禦崇元殿受朝賀。

translations.literal: On wushen, the winter solstice, the emperor attended Chongyuan Hall to receive congratulatory audiences.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, the winter solstice, the emperor held court at Chongyuan Hall to receive the seasonal congratulations.

sentences.zh: 是月，北面行營招討使杜威率諸將領大軍自鄴北征，師次瀛州城下，貝州節度使梁漢璋戰死。

translations.literal: That month, Du Wei, Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Campaign Headquarters, led the generals and a great army north from Ye on campaign; the army halted below the walls of Yingzhou, and Liang Hanzhang, Military Governor of Beizhou, died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Du Wei, commander of the northern campaign, marched north from Ye at the head of the main army; when the force halted beneath Yingzhou, Liang Hanzhang, military governor of Beizhou, was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 杜威等以漢璋之敗，遂收軍而退。

translations.literal: Because of Hanzhang's defeat, Du Wei and the others thereupon withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: After Hanzhang's defeat, Du Wei and his commanders pulled the army back.

sentences.zh: 行次武強，聞契丹入寇，欲取直路，自冀、貝而南。

translations.literal: Marching to Wuqiang, they heard that the Khitan had invaded and wished to take the direct route south through Ji and Bei.
translations.idiomatic: When the column reached Wuqiang and learned that the Khitan had invaded, they intended to march south by the direct route through Ji and Bei.

sentences.zh: 會張彥澤領騎自鎮定至，且言契丹可破之狀，於是大軍西趨鎮州。

translations.literal: Just then Zhang Yanzhe arrived from Zhen and Ding leading cavalry and reported that the Khitan could be defeated, whereupon the great army turned west toward Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanzhe then arrived from Zhen and Ding with cavalry, assuring them that the Khitan could be beaten, and the main army wheeled west toward Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁巳朔，

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, dingsi,
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month, dingsi,

sentences.zh: （案：以下有闕文。

translations.literal: (Note: There is missing text below.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: Text is missing below.

sentences.zh: 據《通鑒》云：丁巳朔，李穀自書密奏，且言大軍危急之勢，請車駕幸滑州，遣高行周、符彥卿扈從，及發兵守澶州、河陽，以備敵之奔沖。

translations.literal: According to Zizhi Tongjian: On dingsi, the first day, Li Gu personally wrote a secret memorial describing the army's grave peril, requesting that the imperial carriage proceed to Huazhou, that Gao Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing escort it, and that troops be sent to hold Chanzhou and Heyang against the enemy's sudden thrust.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian reports that on dingsi, Li Gu wrote a secret memorial in his own hand describing how desperate the army's position had become. He urged the emperor to move to Huazhou with Gao Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing as escorts, and to dispatch troops to hold Chanzhou and Heyang against a sudden enemy thrust.

sentences.zh: 遣軍將關勛走馬上之。）〉

translations.literal: He sent the officer Guan Xun to deliver it at a gallop.)]
translations.idiomatic: He sent the officer Guan Xun to deliver it at a gallop.)]

sentences.zh: 己未，杜威奏，駐軍於中渡橋。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Du Wei memorialized that the army was encamped at Zhongdu Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Du Wei reported that his army was encamped at Zhongdu Bridge.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以前司農卿儲延英為太子賓客。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Chu Yanying, former Minister of Agriculture, was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the former Minister of Agriculture, Chu Yanying, was appointed Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 詔徐州符彥卿屯澶州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou to garrison Chanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou was ordered to garrison Chanzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，詔澤潞、鄴都、邢洺、河陽運糧赴中渡，杜威遣人口奏軍前事宜，勢迫故也。

translations.literal: On xinyou, an edict ordered Ze-Lu, Ye, Xing-Ming, and Heyang to transport grain to Zhongdu; Du Wei sent a messenger to report orally on affairs at the front because the situation was pressing.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Ze-Lu, Ye, Xing-Ming, and Heyang were ordered to ship grain to Zhongdu; Du Wei sent a courier to report orally from the front because the crisis left no time for written memorials.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，又遣高行周屯澶州，景延廣守河陽。

translations.literal: On renxu, Gao Xingzhou was again sent to garrison Chanzhou, and Jing Yanguang to hold Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Gao Xingzhou was again posted to Chanzhou and Jing Yanguang assigned to defend Heyang.

sentences.zh: 博野縣都監張鵬入奏蕃軍事勢。

translations.literal: Zhang Peng, Commandant of Boye County, entered court to report on the barbarian army's situation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Peng, commandant of Boye County, came to court with a report on the Khitan forces.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，定州李殷奏，前月二十八日夜，領捉生四百人往曲陽嘉山下，逢敵軍車帳，殺千餘人，獲馬二百匹。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Li Yin of Dingzhou memorialized that on the night of the twenty-eighth of the previous month he had led four hundred scouts to the foot of Jia Mountain in Quyang, encountered enemy carts and tents, killed more than a thousand men, and captured two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Li Yin of Dingzhou reported that on the night of the twenty-eighth of the previous month he had led four hundred scouts to Jia Mountain below Quyang, surprised an enemy encampment, killed more than a thousand men, and seized two hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 詔宋州高行周充北面行營都部署，符彥卿充副，邢州方太充都虞候，領後軍駐於河上，以備敵騎之奔沖也。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Gao Xingzhou of Songzhou Overall Commander of the Northern Campaign Headquarters, with Fu Yanqing as deputy and Fang Tai of Xingzhou as Chief Controller, to lead the rear army and garrison the river line against the enemy cavalry's sudden thrust.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou of Songzhou was made overall commander of the northern campaign, with Fu Yanqing as his deputy and Fang Tai of Xingzhou as chief controller; they were to hold the rear army along the river against a sudden Khitan cavalry thrust.

sentences.zh: 時契丹遊騎涉滹水而南，至欒城縣。

translations.literal: At that time Khitan patrol cavalry crossed the Hutuo River southward as far as Luancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan patrols had crossed the Hutuo south as far as Luancheng County.

sentences.zh: 自是中渡寨為蕃軍隔絕，探報不通，朝廷大恐，故委行周等繼領兵師守扼津要，且以張其勢也。

translations.literal: From then on the Zhongdu camp was cut off by the barbarian army and scouts could not get through; the court was greatly alarmed, and therefore entrusted Xingzhou and the others in succession with troops to hold the strategic crossings and also to display greater strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongdu camp was now cut off from the capital, and no scouts could get through. The court was terrified and therefore sent Xingzhou and the others in turn to hold the key crossings—and to make a show of strength.

sentences.zh: 己巳，邢州方太奏，此月六日，契丹與王師戰於中渡，王師不利，奉國都指揮使王清戰死。

translations.literal: On jisi, Fang Tai of Xingzhou memorialized that on the sixth of this month the Khitan fought the imperial army at Zhongdu; the imperial army fared badly, and Wang Qing, Commander-in-Chief of Fengguo, died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Fang Tai of Xingzhou reported that on the sixth the Khitan had fought the imperial army at Zhongdu; the imperial forces were beaten, and Wang Qing, commander of Fengguo, was killed.

sentences.zh: 庚午，幸沙臺射兔。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the emperor visited Shatai to hunt hares.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the emperor went to Shatai to hunt hares.

sentences.zh: 壬申，始聞杜威、李守貞等以此月十日率諸軍降於契丹。

translations.literal: On renshen, word first arrived that on the tenth of this month Du Wei, Li Shouzhen, and the others had led all the armies in surrender to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, the court first learned that on the tenth Du Wei, Li Shouzhen, and the rest had surrendered the entire army to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 是夜，相州節度使張彥澤受契丹命，率先鋒二千人，自封丘門斬關而入。

translations.literal: That night, Zhang Yanzhe, Military Governor of Xiangzhou, acting on Khitan orders, led two thousand vanguard troops, cut through the gate at Fengqiu Gate, and entered.
translations.idiomatic: That night, Zhang Yanzhe of Xiangzhou, acting on Khitan orders, led two thousand vanguard troops through Fengqiu Gate after cutting down the guards.

sentences.zh: 癸酉旦，張彥澤頓兵於明德門外，京城大擾。

translations.literal: At dawn on guiyou, Zhang Yanzhe stationed troops outside Mingde Gate, and the capital was thrown into great turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on guiyou, Zhang Yanzhe halted his troops outside Mingde Gate, and the capital erupted in chaos.

sentences.zh: 前曹州節度使石赟死，帝之堂叔也。

translations.literal: Shi Yun, former Military Governor of Caozhou, died; he was the emperor's paternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yun, former military governor of Caozhou and the emperor's paternal uncle, died.

sentences.zh: 時自中渡寨隔絕之後，帝與大臣端坐憂危，國之衛兵，悉在北面，計無所出。

translations.literal: From the time the Zhongdu camp was cut off, the emperor and his ministers sat upright in anxiety and peril; all the empire's guard troops were in the north, and no plan could be found.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhongdu camp was cut off, the emperor and his ministers sat helpless in dread; every soldier of the imperial guard was in the north, and no plan offered itself.

sentences.zh: 十六日聞滹水之降。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth they heard of the surrender at the Hutuo.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth came word of the surrender at the Hutuo.

sentences.zh: 是夜，偵知張彥澤已至滑州，召李崧、馮玉、李彥韜入內計事，方議詔河東劉知遠起兵赴難，至五鼓初，張彥澤引蕃騎入京。

translations.literal: That night, scouts learned that Zhang Yanzhe had reached Huazhou; Li Song, Feng Yu, and Li Yantao were summoned within to deliberate. They had just begun discussing an edict for Liu Zhiyuan of Hedong to raise troops to the rescue when, at the first watch of the fifth watch, Zhang Yanzhe led barbarian cavalry into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That night scouts reported Zhang Yanzhe at Huazhou. Li Song, Feng Yu, and Li Yantao were called in to counsel the throne; they were debating an edict to Liu Zhiyuan in Hedong to march to the rescue when, at the fifth watch, Zhang Yanzhe rode into the capital at the head of Khitan cavalry.

sentences.zh: 宮中相次火起，帝自攜劍驅擁后妃已下十數人，將同赴火，為親校薛超所持。

translations.literal: Fires broke out one after another in the palace; the emperor himself took a sword and drove more than ten people including the empress and consorts, intending to enter the flames together, but was seized and held by his personal officer Xue Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Fires broke out throughout the palace. The emperor drew his sword and drove the empress, his consorts, and more than a dozen attendants toward the flames, intending to die with them, but his personal guard Xue Chao seized and restrained him.

sentences.zh: 俄自寬仁門遞入契丹主與皇太后書，帝乃止，旋令撲滅煙火。

translations.literal: Shortly a letter from the Khitan lord and the empress dowager was delivered through Kuanren Gate; the emperor then stopped, and immediately ordered the fires extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a letter from the Khitan emperor and the empress dowager was delivered through Kuanren Gate. The emperor desisted and ordered the fires put out.

sentences.zh: 大內都點檢康福全在寬仁門宿衛，登樓覘賊，彥澤呼而下之。

translations.literal: Kang Fuquan, Chief Inspector of the Inner Palace, was on night guard at Kuanren Gate; he climbed a tower to spy on the enemy, and Yanzhe called him down.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Fuquan, chief inspector of the inner palace, was on guard at Kuanren Gate. He climbed a tower to watch the enemy, and Yanzhe summoned him down.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，帝奉表於戎主曰：

translations.literal: On guiyou, the emperor submitted a memorial to the Khitan lord, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the emperor submitted this memorial to the Khitan lord:

sentences.zh: 孫臣某言：今月十七日寅時，相州節度使張彥澤、都監傅住兒部領大軍入京，賫到翁皇帝賜太后書示，於滹沱河降下杜重威一行馬步兵士，見領蕃漢步騎來幸汴州者。

translations.literal: Your grandson-subject speaks: At the yin hour on the seventeenth of this month, Zhang Yanzhe, Military Governor of Xiangzhou, and the Commandant Fu Zhu'er led a great army into the capital and presented the letter that Grandfather Emperor bestowed on the empress dowager, showing that at the Hutuo River Du Chongwei's entire force of cavalry and infantry had surrendered and that Khitan and Han foot and horse now advancing to favor Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Your grandson humbly reports: At the yin hour on the seventeenth of this month, Zhang Yanzhe of Xiangzhou and Commandant Fu Zhu'er entered the capital at the head of a great army bearing the letter Grandfather Emperor had sent the empress dowager. It showed that Du Chongwei's entire army had surrendered at the Hutuo and that Khitan and Han infantry and cavalry were now marching on Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 往者，唐運告終，中原失馭，數窮否極，天缺地傾。

translations.literal: Formerly, the fortune of Tang came to an end; the Central Plains lost control; number reached its limit and adversity its extreme; heaven cracked and earth tilted.
translations.idiomatic: In former days the mandate of Tang expired; the Central Plains lost their ruler; fate had run its course and ruin was complete, as if heaven and earth themselves were breaking apart.

sentences.zh: 先人有田一成，有眾一旅，兵連禍結，力屈勢孤。

translations.literal: My forebear held a single district of land and a single brigade of men; war linked with calamity, strength bent and position isolated.
translations.idiomatic: My forebear held barely a single district and a single brigade; war piled upon disaster until his strength was spent and he stood alone.

sentences.zh: 翁皇帝救患摧鋒，興利除害，躬擐甲胄，深入寇場。

translations.literal: Grandfather Emperor rescued from calamity and crushed the enemy van, promoted benefit and removed harm, personally donned armor, and penetrated deep into the enemy field.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Emperor came to our rescue, shattered the enemy's van, and worked for the people's good; he himself buckled on armor and plunged deep into the field of battle.

sentences.zh: 犯露蒙霜，度雁門之險；

translations.literal: He braved dew and bore frost, crossed the peril of Yanmen;
translations.idiomatic: He endured dew and frost and crossed the peril of Yanmen Pass;

sentences.zh: 馳風掣電，行中冀之誅。

translations.literal: he raced like wind and lightning and carried out the punishment in central Ji.
translations.idiomatic: he swept like wind and lightning to execute justice in central Ji.

sentences.zh: 黃鉞一麾，天下大定。

translations.literal: At one wave of the golden axe, the realm was greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: At a single wave of the battle-axe, the realm was pacified.

sentences.zh: 勢淩宇宙，義感神明，功成不居，遂興晉祚，則翁皇帝有大造於石氏也。

translations.literal: His power overawed the cosmos; his righteousness moved the spirits; achieving merit he did not keep it, and thus raised the Jin throne—so Grandfather Emperor wrought great creation for the House of Shi.
translations.idiomatic: His might overawed heaven and earth; his righteousness moved the spirits. He achieved victory yet claimed no glory, and in doing so raised the Jin throne. Grandfather Emperor thus bestowed a great founding gift upon the House of Shi.

sentences.zh: 旋屬天降鞠兇，先君即世，臣遵承遺旨，纘紹前基。

translations.literal: Soon heaven sent grievous calamity; my late father passed away, and I, following his testament, continued the former foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon heaven sent fresh calamity: my late father died, and I, obeying his final charge, took up the foundation he had laid.

sentences.zh: 諒暗之初，荒迷失次，凡有軍國重事，皆委將相大臣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of my mourning seclusion I was confused and lost in propriety; all weighty affairs of army and state were entrusted to the generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first days of mourning I was lost and disordered; every weighty matter of army and state I left to my generals and ministers.

sentences.zh: 至於擅繼宗祧，既非稟命；

translations.literal: As for seizing succession to the ancestral temple on my own, it was not by received command;
translations.idiomatic: As for seizing the succession on my own authority, I had received no command to do so;

sentences.zh: 輕發文字，輒敢抗尊。

translations.literal: issuing documents lightly, I dared again and again to resist your exalted authority.
translations.idiomatic: and in issuing edicts lightly I repeatedly defied your exalted will.

sentences.zh: 自啟釁端，果貽赫怒，禍至神惑，運盡天亡。

translations.literal: Having myself opened the cause of strife, I indeed incurred your thunderous wrath; calamity arrived and the spirits were confounded; fortune was exhausted and heaven decreed extinction.
translations.idiomatic: I myself provoked this war and truly earned your thunderous wrath. Calamity fell, the spirits themselves were confounded, my fortune ran out, and heaven decreed my end.

sentences.zh: 十萬師徒，皆望風而束手；

translations.literal: A hundred thousand officers and men all, at sight of the wind, bound their hands;
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand soldiers laid down their arms at the first rumor of your approach;

sentences.zh: 億兆黎庶，悉延頸以歸心。

translations.literal: the millions of common people all stretched their necks to turn their hearts homeward.
translations.idiomatic: and countless common people craned their necks in longing for your rule.

sentences.zh: 臣負義包羞，貪生忍恥，自貽顛覆，上累祖宗，偷度晨昏，茍存食息。

translations.literal: Your subject bears guilt wrapped in shame, clinging to life and enduring disgrace, bringing ruin upon himself and burdening his ancestors above, stealing through dawn and dusk and barely preserving breath and food.
translations.idiomatic: I have betrayed my duty and wrapped myself in shame, clinging to life and enduring disgrace. I brought ruin on myself and shamed my ancestors, stealing through each day merely to keep breathing.

sentences.zh: 翁皇帝若惠顧疇昔，稍霽雷霆，未賜靈誅，不絕先祀，則百口荷更生之德，一門銜無報之恩，雖所願焉，非敢望也。

translations.literal: If Grandfather Emperor in kindness recalls former days, slightly clears his thunder, does not bestow divine execution, and does not cut off the ancestral sacrifices, then a hundred mouths would bear the grace of renewed life and one household would carry a debt of gratitude beyond repayment—though this is what I wish, I dare not hope for it.
translations.idiomatic: If Grandfather Emperor would look back on former ties, temper his wrath, withhold the death I deserve, and let our ancestral rites continue, a hundred mouths would owe him the gift of new life and our whole house a debt we could never repay. That is my deepest wish, though I dare not expect it.

sentences.zh: 臣與太后並妻馮氏及舉家戚屬，見於郊野面縛俟罪次。

translations.literal: Your subject, together with the empress dowager, my wife Lady Feng, and all kinsmen of the household, await in the suburbs with faces bound, awaiting judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager, my wife Lady Feng, our kinsmen, and I wait in the suburbs with bound hands, ready to receive judgment.

sentences.zh: 所有國寶一面、金印三面，今遣長子陜府節度使延煦、次子曹州節度使延寶管押進納，並奉表請罪，陳謝以聞。

translations.literal: There is one imperial treasure seal and three golden seals; I now send my eldest son Yanshu, Military Governor of Shan Prefecture, and my second son Yanbao, Military Governor of Cao Prefecture, to escort and present them, and together submit this memorial begging pardon, declaring my repentance for your hearing.
translations.idiomatic: I send one imperial seal and three golden seals, escorted by my eldest son Yanshu, military governor of Shan, and my second son Yanbao, military governor of Cao, together with this memorial begging your pardon.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，張彥澤遷帝與太后及諸宮屬於開封府，遣控鶴指揮使李榮將兵監守。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Zhang Yanzhe moved the emperor, the empress dowager, and all palace dependents to the Kaifeng prefectural office and sent Li Rong, Commander of the Crane-Control Guard, with troops to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Zhang Yanzhe transferred the emperor, the empress dowager, and the palace household to the Kaifeng prefectural yamen and posted Li Rong of the Crane-Control Guard with troops to keep watch.

sentences.zh: 是夜，開封尹桑維翰、宣徽使孟承誨皆遇害。

translations.literal: That night, Sang Weihan, Prefect of Kaifeng, and Meng Chenghui, Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: That night Sang Weihan, prefect of Kaifeng, and Meng Chenghui, palace commissioner, were murdered.

sentences.zh: 帝以契丹主將至，欲與太后出迎，彥澤先表之，稟契丹主之旨報云：「比欲許爾朝覲上國，臣僚奏言，豈有兩個天子道路相見！

translations.literal: Because the Khitan lord was about to arrive, the emperor wished to go out with the empress dowager to welcome him; Yanzhe memorialized first and reported the Khitan lord's decree: "We had intended to allow you to pay court in the superior state, but the ministers memorialized, saying, How can two Sons of Heaven meet on the road!
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan emperor was expected, the emperor wished to go out with the empress dowager to welcome him. Yanzhe reported the Khitan reply in advance: "We had meant to let you pay court in our realm, but our ministers objected: how can two Sons of Heaven meet on the road?

sentences.zh: 今賜所佩刀子，以慰爾心。

translations.literal: We now bestow the knife you wear at your belt to comfort your heart.
translations.idiomatic: We now give you the knife at your belt to comfort you.

sentences.zh: 」己卯，皇子延煦、延寶自帳中回，得敵詔慰撫，帝表謝之。

translations.literal: On jimao, the princes Yanshu and Yanbao returned from the enemy camp with an edict of consolation; the emperor submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Yanshu and Yanbao returned from the Khitan camp with a message of reassurance, and the emperor sent a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 時契丹主以所送傳國寶制造非工，與載籍所述者異，使人來問。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan lord, because the transmitted imperial treasure sent was crudely made and differed from what the records described, sent a man to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor found the seal they had sent poorly made and unlike the descriptions in the classics, and sent an envoy to question them.

sentences.zh: 帝進狀曰：「頃以偽主王從珂於洛京大內自焚之後，其真傳國寶不知所在，必是當時焚之。

translations.literal: The emperor submitted a statement saying: "Recently, after the false ruler Wang Congke burned himself in the great inner palace at Luoyang, the true transmitted imperial treasure was nowhere to be found and must have been burned at that time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "After the usurper Wang Congke burned himself in the Luoyang palace, the true imperial seal vanished and was surely destroyed in that fire.

sentences.zh: 先帝受命，旋制此寶，在位臣僚，備知其事。

translations.literal: When my late father received the mandate, he promptly had this treasure made; the officials then in office all know the matter fully.
translations.idiomatic: When my late father took the throne he had this seal made at once; every minister then in office knows it.

sentences.zh: 臣至今日，敢有隱藏」云。

translations.literal: Down to today your subject would not dare conceal anything," he said.
translations.idiomatic: To this day I would not dare conceal anything," he said.

sentences.zh: 時移內庫至府，帝使人取帛數段，主者不與，謂使者曰：「此非我所有也。

translations.literal: When the inner treasury was moved to the prefectural office, the emperor sent someone to take several lengths of silk; the custodian would not give them and told the messenger, "These are no longer mine.
translations.idiomatic: When the inner treasury was moved to the prefectural yamen, the emperor sent for several lengths of silk; the keeper refused, telling the messenger, "These are no longer mine.

sentences.zh: 」又使人詣李崧求酒，崧曰：「臣有酒非敢愛惜，慮陛下杯酌之後憂躁，所作別有不測之事，臣以此不敢奉進。

translations.literal: The emperor also sent someone to Li Song to ask for wine. Song said, "Your subject has wine and would not begrudge it, but I fear that after Your Majesty drinks a cup, in grief and agitation you might do something else unforeseen; for this reason I dare not present it.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent to Li Song for wine. Song said, "I have wine and do not begrudge it, but I fear that after you drink, grief may drive you to some desperate act. For that reason I dare not send it.

sentences.zh: 」丙戌晦，百官宿封禪寺。

translations.literal: On bingxu, the last day of the month, the hundred officials lodged at Fengchan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, the last day of the month, the officials lodged at Fengchan Temple.

sentences.zh: 明年正月朔，契丹主次東京城北。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the following year, the Khitan lord halted north of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the following year, the Khitan emperor made camp north of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 百官列班，遙辭帝於寺，詣北郊以迎契丹主。

translations.literal: The hundred officials formed ranks, took leave of the emperor at a distance at the temple, and went to the northern suburbs to welcome the Khitan lord.
translations.idiomatic: The officials formed ranks at the temple, bade the emperor farewell from afar, and went to the northern suburbs to welcome the Khitan emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝舉族出封丘門，肩轝至野，契丹主不與之見，遣泊封禪寺。

translations.literal: The emperor led his entire clan out through Fengqiu Gate, was carried on shoulders in a litter to the open field, but the Khitan lord would not meet him and sent him to lodge at Fengchan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led his whole clan out through Fengqiu Gate and was carried in a litter to the open field, but the Khitan emperor refused to see him and had him lodged at Fengchan Temple.

sentences.zh: 文武百官素服紗帽，迎謁契丹主於郊次，俯伏俟罪，契丹主命起之，親自慰撫。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials in plain dress and gauze caps welcomed and paid court to the Khitan lord at the suburban station, prostrating themselves to await punishment; the Khitan lord ordered them raised and personally comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials in plain dress and gauze caps met the Khitan emperor at the suburban station, prostrating themselves to await judgment. He ordered them raised and personally reassured them.

sentences.zh: 契丹主遂入大內，至昏出宮，是夜宿於赤堈。

translations.literal: The Khitan lord then entered the great inner palace, left at dusk, and that night lodged at Chijin.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor then entered the inner palace, left at dusk, and that night lodged at Chijin.

sentences.zh: 偽詔應晉朝臣僚一切仍舊，朝廷儀制並用漢禮。

translations.literal: A spurious edict responded that Jin dynasty officials should all remain as before, and court ritual should all use Han rites.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that Jin officials would remain in their posts and that court ritual would follow Han custom.

sentences.zh: 戊子，殺鄭州防禦使楊承勛，責以背父之罪，令左右臠割而死。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Yang Chengxun, Defender of Zhengzhou, was killed; charged with the crime of betraying his father, he was ordered dismembered by those at hand until dead.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Yang Chengxun, defender of Zhengzhou, was executed for betraying his father; his attendants hacked him to pieces until he died.

sentences.zh: （《遼史》：以其弟承信為平盧軍節度使，襲父爵。）〉

translations.literal: (Liao History: His younger brother Chengxin was made Military Governor of Pinglu Army and inherited his father's title.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Liao History: His younger brother Chengxin was appointed military governor of Pinglu and inherited their father's title.)]

sentences.zh: 己丑，斬張彥澤於市，以其剽劫京城，恣行屠害也。

translations.literal: On jichou, Zhang Yanzhe was beheaded in the market because he had plundered the capital and wantonly carried out slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Zhang Yanzhe was beheaded in the market for plundering the capital and slaughtering its people without restraint.

sentences.zh: （《遼史》云：以張彥澤擅徙重貴開封，殺桑維翰，縱兵大掠，不道，斬於市。）〉

translations.literal: (Liao History says: Because Zhang Yanzhe on his own authority moved Chonggui to Kaifeng, killed Sang Weihan, and let his troops plunder on a great scale—conduct beyond the Way—he was beheaded in the market.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Liao History: Zhang Yanzhe was beheaded in the market for unlawfully transferring Chonggui to Kaifeng, killing Sang Weihan, and letting his troops loot the city.)]

sentences.zh: 庚寅，洛京留守景延廣自扼吭而死。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Jing Yanguang, Military Governor of Luoyang, died by strangling his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Jing Yanguang, military governor of Luoyang, took his own life by strangling.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，契丹制，降帝為光祿大夫、檢校太尉，封負義侯，黃龍府安置。

translations.literal: On xinmao, by Khitan decree the emperor was demoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Grand Marshal by Inspection, enfeoffed as Marquis Who Bears Guilt, and settled at Huanglong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the Khitan emperor demoted him to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Grand Marshal by Inspection, enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Bears Guilt, and sent him to live at Huanglong.

sentences.zh: 其地在渤海國界。

translations.literal: That place lay within the borders of the Bohai state.
translations.idiomatic: That region lay within what had been Bohai territory.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，遷帝於封禪寺，遣蕃大將崔廷勛將兵守之。

translations.literal: On guisi, the emperor was moved to Fengchan Temple, and the barbarian general Cui Tingxun was sent with troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, the emperor was moved to Fengchan Temple under guard by the Khitan general Cui Tingxun.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，帝與皇太后李氏、皇太妃安氏、皇后馮氏、皇弟重睿、皇子延煦延寶俱北行，以宮嬪五十人、內官三十人、東西班五十人、醫官一人、控鶴官四人、禦廚七人、茶酒三人、儀鸞司三人、軍健二十人從行。

translations.literal: On guimao, the emperor, together with Empress Dowager Lady Li, Grand Imperial Consort Lady An, Empress Lady Feng, his younger brother Chongrui, and the princes Yanshu and Yanbao, all traveled north, accompanied by fifty palace women, thirty inner eunuchs, fifty officials of the eastern and western shifts, one medical officer, four Crane-Control officers, seven imperial kitchen staff, three tea and wine attendants, three Ritual Phoenix Bureau staff, and twenty military guards.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, the emperor set out north with Empress Dowager Li, Grand Imperial Consort An, Empress Feng, his brother Chongrui, and Princes Yanshu and Yanbao, attended by fifty palace women, thirty inner eunuchs, fifty court officials, one physician, four Crane-Control officers, seven imperial cooks, three tea and wine servants, three from the Ritual Phoenix Bureau, and twenty guards.

sentences.zh: 宰臣趙瑩、樞密使馮玉、侍衛馬軍都指揮使李彥韜隨帝入蕃，契丹主遣三百騎援送而去。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhao Ying, Commissioner Feng Yu, and Li Yantao, Commander of the Palace Horse Army of the Imperial Guard, accompanied the emperor into the barbarian lands; the Khitan lord sent three hundred cavalry to escort them on their way.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhao Ying, Commissioner Feng Yu, and Li Yantao, commander of the imperial guard cavalry, accompanied the emperor into Khitan territory while three hundred Khitan horsemen escorted the party north.

sentences.zh: 所經州郡，長吏迎奉，皆為契丹主阻絕，有所供饋亦不通。

translations.literal: In every prefecture and commandery they passed, the chief officials came out to welcome and serve them, but all were blocked by the Khitan lord, and whatever supplies were offered could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they passed, local officials tried to welcome and provision them, but the Khitan emperor blocked every approach, and no supplies could reach the exiled court.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·李穀傳》：少帝蒙塵而北，舊臣無敢候謁者，穀獨拜迎於路，君臣相對泣下。

translations.literal: (Song History, Biography of Li Gu: When the Young Emperor suffered exile and went north, none of the former ministers dared to wait upon and visit him; Gu alone bowed in welcome on the road, and ruler and subject wept facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: (Song History, Biography of Li Gu: When the Young Emperor was driven north into exile, none of his former ministers dared pay their respects; Li Gu alone bowed to him on the road, and emperor and subject wept face to face.

sentences.zh: 穀曰：「臣無狀，負陛下。

translations.literal: Gu said, "Your subject is without merit and has failed Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "I have been worthless and have failed Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」因傾囊以獻。）〉

translations.literal: He thereupon emptied his purse and presented it.)]
translations.idiomatic: Then he emptied his purse and offered everything he had.)]

sentences.zh: 嘗一日，帝與太后不能得食，乃殺畜而啖之。

translations.literal: On one occasion the emperor and the empress dowager could obtain no food and so killed livestock and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor and the empress dowager could get no food at all and had to slaughter their livestock to eat.

sentences.zh: 帝過中渡橋，閱前杜威營寨之跡，慨然憤嘆，謂左右曰：「我家何負，為此賊所破，天乎！

translations.literal: When the emperor passed Zhongdu Bridge and surveyed the traces of Du Wei's former camp, he sighed in indignant lament and said to those beside him, "What fault has my house committed, that this traitor should destroy us—O Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Crossing Zhongdu Bridge, the emperor looked over the ruins of Du Wei's camp and cried out in bitter anger to his attendants, "What have we done to deserve ruin at the hands of this traitor? O Heaven!

sentences.zh: 天乎！

translations.literal: O Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: O Heaven!

sentences.zh: 」於是號慟而去。

translations.literal: He then wailed and went on his way.
translations.idiomatic: Then he wailed aloud and moved on.

sentences.zh: 至幽州，傾城士庶迎看於路，見帝慘沮，無不嗟嘆。

translations.literal: When he reached Youzhou, the whole city's gentry and commoners came out to the road to look; seeing the emperor's wretched dejection, none failed to sigh in lament.
translations.idiomatic: At Youzhou the whole city turned out along the road to watch; when they saw the emperor's wretched state, everyone sighed in grief.

sentences.zh: （《宣政雜錄》：徽宗北狩，經薊縣梁魚務，有還鄉橋，石少帝所命名也，里人至今呼之。）〉

translations.literal: (Miscellaneous Records of Xuanzheng's Reign: When Huizong was taken north on campaign, he passed Liangyu Post in Ji County, where there is a Bridge of Returning Home, named by the Young Emperor of Shi; the villagers still call it that today.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Miscellaneous Records of Xuanzheng's Reign: When Huizong was marched north, he passed Liangyu Post in Ji County, where there is a Bridge of Returning Home, named by the Later Jin Young Emperor; locals still use that name today.)]

sentences.zh: 駐留旬餘，州將承契丹命，犒帝於府署，趙延壽母以食饌來獻。

translations.literal: He halted for more than ten days; the prefectural commander, acting on Khitan orders, entertained the emperor at the government office, and Zhao Yanshou's mother came to present food.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed more than ten days while the prefect, on Khitan orders, entertained him at the yamen; Zhao Yanshou's mother brought food as a gift.

sentences.zh: 自范陽行數十程，過薊州、平州，至榆關沙塞之地，略無供給，每至宿頓，無非路次，一行乏食，宮女、從官但采木實野蔬，以救饑弊。

translations.literal: From Fanyang he traveled several tens of stages, passing Jizhou and Pingzhou to the sandy frontier at Yuguan, with almost no supplies; at every halt there was nothing but the roadside, and the whole party lacked food; palace women and attendant officials could only gather tree fruit and wild vegetables to relieve their hunger and exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: From Fanyang they marched dozens of stages through Jizhou and Pingzhou to the sandy frontier at Yuguan, with almost nothing to eat. At every halt they camped by the roadside; palace women and attendants gathered wild fruit and vegetables to stave off starvation.

sentences.zh: 又行七八日至錦州，契丹迫帝與妃後往拜安巴堅遺像，帝不勝屈辱，泣曰：「薛超誤我，不令我死，以至今日也。

translations.literal: After another seven or eight days they reached Jinzhou; the Khitan forced the emperor and the consorts to go pay homage to the portrait of the late Ambaqian. The emperor could not bear the humiliation and wept, saying, "Xue Chao wronged me by not letting me die, and so it has come to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Seven or eight days later they reached Jinzhou, where the Khitan forced the emperor and his consorts to bow before the portrait of the late Ambaqian. Overwhelmed with shame, he wept, "Xue Chao was wrong to keep me from dying—I have lived to see this day.

sentences.zh: 」又行數十程，渡遼水，至黃龍府，即此所命安置之地也。

translations.literal: After another several tens of stages they crossed the Liao River and reached Huanglong Prefecture—the very place where he had been ordered to settle.
translations.idiomatic: After many more stages they crossed the Liao River and reached Huanglong—the very place to which he had been exiled.

sentences.zh: 六月，契丹國母召帝一行往懷密州，州在黃龍府西北千戎王裏。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Khitan empress dowager summoned the emperor's party to go to Huaimi Prefecture, which lay more than a thousand li northwest of Huanglong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Khitan empress dowager summoned the exiled court to Huaimi Prefecture, more than a thousand li northwest of Huanglong.

sentences.zh: 行至遼陽，皇后馮氏以帝陷蕃，過受艱苦，令內官潛求毒藥，將自飲之，並以進帝，不果而止。

translations.literal: When they reached Liaoyang, Empress Lady Feng, because the emperor had fallen into the barbarian lands and suffered excessive hardship, ordered an inner eunuch secretly to seek poison, intending to drink it herself and also present it to the emperor; the plan did not succeed and was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: At Liaoyang, Empress Feng, seeing how the emperor had suffered in Khitan captivity, secretly sent a eunuch to obtain poison so that she might kill herself and offer it to him as well; the plan failed and was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 又行二百里，會國母為永康王所執，永康王請帝卻往遼陽城駐泊，帝遣使奉表於永康，且賀克捷，自是帝一行稍得供給。

translations.literal: After another two hundred li, they learned that the empress dowager had been seized by Prince Yongkang; Prince Yongkang asked the emperor to return and halt at Liaoyang city. The emperor sent an envoy with a memorial to Yongkang and also to congratulate him on his victory; from then on the emperor's party gradually obtained supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred li farther on they learned that the Khitan empress dowager had been seized by Prince Yongkang, who invited the emperor to lodge again at Liaoyang. The emperor sent a memorial congratulating him on his victory, and from then on the exiled court began to receive supplies again.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐二年二月，帝自遼陽城發赴建州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Qianyou of Han, the emperor set out from Liaoyang city for Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Han Qianyou year 2, the emperor left Liaoyang for Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 行至中路，太妃安氏得疾而薨，乃焚之，載其燼骨而行。

translations.literal: Midway on the journey Grand Imperial Consort Lady An fell ill and died; they cremated her and carried her ashes as they went.
translations.idiomatic: Midway on the journey Grand Imperial Consort An fell ill and died; they cremated her and carried her ashes with them.

sentences.zh: 帝自遼陽行十數日，過儀州、灞州，遂至建州。

translations.literal: From Liaoyang the emperor traveled more than ten days, passing Yizhou and Bazhou, and then reached Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: From Liaoyang he traveled more than ten days through Yizhou and Bazhou before reaching Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 節度使趙延暉盡禮奉迎，館帝於衙署中。

translations.literal: The Military Governor Zhao Yanhui welcomed him with full ceremony and lodged the emperor in the government office.
translations.idiomatic: Military Governor Zhao Yanhui received him with full ceremony and lodged him in the prefectural yamen.

sentences.zh: 其後割寨地五千餘頃，其地至建州數十里。

translations.literal: Later more than five thousand qing of stockade land was allotted; the land extended several tens of li to Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later they were granted more than five thousand qing of frontier land, reaching to within several tens of li of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝乃令一行人員於寨地內築室分耕，給食於帝。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered the members of his party to build houses within the stockade land and divide the fields for cultivation, providing food for the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had his party build houses on the allotted land, divide the fields, and farm them to feed the exiled court.

sentences.zh: 是歲，述律王子遣契丹數騎詣帝，取內人趙氏、聶氏疾馳而去。

translations.literal: That year a prince of the Shulü clan sent several Khitan horsemen to the emperor, seized the inner attendants Lady Zhao and Lady Nie, and galloped away with them.
translations.idiomatic: That year a prince of the Shulü clan sent Khitan horsemen who seized the emperor's favorites Lady Zhao and Lady Nie and rode off with them.

sentences.zh: 趙、聶者，帝之寵姬也，及其被奪，不勝悲憤。

translations.literal: Zhao and Nie were the emperor's favored consorts; when they were taken away, he could not overcome his grief and rage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao and Nie were his favorite consorts; when they were taken from him, his grief and anger were beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐三年八月，太后薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Qianyou of Han, the empress dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Han Qianyou year 3, the empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，有漢人自塞北而至者，言帝與後及諸子俱無恙，猶在建州，其隨從職官役使人輩，自蕃中亡歸，物故者大半矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande of Zhou, a Han man came from north of the frontier and said that the emperor, the empress, and all the sons were unharmed and still at Jianzhou; of the attendant officials, clerks, and servants, those who had fled back from the barbarian lands numbered mostly among the dead.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhou Xiande, a man returned from beyond the frontier reporting that the emperor, empress, and princes were still alive at Jianzhou; of the officials and servants who had accompanied them, most of those who made it back had died in captivity.

sentences.zh: （《郡齋讀書志》云：《晉朝陷蕃記》，範質撰。

translations.literal: (Junzhai Dushu Zhi says: Record of the Jin Dynasty's Fall among the Barbarians, compiled by Fan Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: (Junzhai Dushu Zhi: Record of the Jin Dynasty's Fall among the Barbarians, by Fan Zhi.

sentences.zh: 質，石晉末在翰林，為出帝草降表，知其事為詳。

translations.literal: Zhi, at the end of Later Jin, was in the Hanlin Academy and drafted the surrender memorial for the Outgoing Emperor; he knew the events in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi had served in the Hanlin at the end of Later Jin and drafted the Outgoing Emperor's surrender memorial, so he knew these events in detail.

sentences.zh: 記少帝初遷於黃龍府，後居於建州，凡十八年而卒。

translations.literal: It records that the Young Emperor was first moved to Huanglong Prefecture, later dwelt at Jianzhou, and after eighteen years in all died.
translations.idiomatic: It records that the Young Emperor was first sent to Huanglong, later lived at Jianzhou, and died after eighteen years in all.

sentences.zh: 案：契丹丙午歲入汴，順數至甲子歲為十八年，實太祖乾德二年也。

translations.literal: Note: In the year bingwu the Khitan entered Bian; counting forward to the year jiazi makes eighteen years, which is in fact the second year of Qiande of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Note: The Khitan entered Bian in bingwu year; counting forward eighteen years to jiazi brings us to Taizu Qiande year 2.

sentences.zh: 《五代史補》：少主之嗣位也，契丹以不俟命而擅立；

translations.literal: Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: When the Young Lord succeeded to the throne, the Khitan, because he had been enthroned without awaiting their command, acted on their own authority;
translations.idiomatic: Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: When the Young Lord took the throne, the Khitan were angered that he had been enthroned without their leave;

sentences.zh: 又，景延廣辱其使。

translations.literal: moreover, Jing Yanguang had insulted their envoy.
translations.idiomatic: and Jing Yanguang had insulted their envoy.

sentences.zh: 契丹怒，舉國南侵。

translations.literal: The Khitan were enraged and invaded south with the whole nation.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the Khitan invaded the south with their whole nation.

sentences.zh: 以駙馬都尉杜重威等領駕下精兵甲禦之於中流渡橋。

translations.literal: Du Chongwei, Chief Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Guard, and others led the elite troops of the imperial guard in armor to resist them at Zhongliu Crossing Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei, Chief Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Guard, and others led the emperor's elite troops to meet them at Zhongliu Crossing Bridge.

sentences.zh: 既而契丹之眾已深入，而重威等奏報未到朝廷。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitan host had penetrated deep, yet the memorial reports of Chongwei and the others had not reached the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan army had already penetrated deep inland, yet no reports from Chongwei and the others had reached the court.

sentences.zh: 時桑維翰罷相，為開封府尹，謂僚佐曰：「事急矣，非大臣鉗口之時。

translations.literal: At that time Sang Weihan had been dismissed as chief minister and was Prefect of Kaifeng; he said to his staff, "The matter is urgent; this is not the time for great ministers to keep silent.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Weihan had been dismissed as chief minister and was serving as prefect of Kaifeng. He told his staff, "The crisis is upon us; this is no time for ministers to hold their tongues.

sentences.zh: 」乃叩內閣求見，欲請車駕親征，以固將士之心。

translations.literal: He then knocked at the inner gate seeking audience, wishing to request that the imperial carriage go on campaign in person to steady the hearts of the officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the inner gate and asked for an audience, urging the emperor to take the field in person to steady the troops.

sentences.zh: 而少主方在後苑調鷹，至暮竟不召。

translations.literal: But the Young Lord was just then in the rear park training hawks and to evening was never summoned.
translations.idiomatic: But the Young Lord was in the rear park training hawks and never summoned him, even by evening.

sentences.zh: 維翰退而嘆曰：「國家阽危如此，草澤逋客亦宜下問，況大臣求見而不召耶！

translations.literal: Weihan withdrew and sighed, saying, "The state is in such peril on the brink; even a fugitive guest from the marshes ought to be questioned from above—how much more when a great minister seeks audience and is not summoned!
translations.idiomatic: Weihan withdrew and sighed, "The state stands on the brink of ruin. Even a fugitive in the marshes ought to be consulted—how much more a chief minister who asks for audience and is refused!

sentences.zh: 事亦可知矣。

translations.literal: The outcome can already be known.
translations.idiomatic: The outcome is already plain.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，杜重威之徒降於契丹，少主遂北遷。）〉

translations.literal: Before long, Du Chongwei and his fellows surrendered to the Khitan, and the Young Lord was thereupon moved north.)]
translations.idiomatic: Before long Du Chongwei and his men surrendered to the Khitan, and the Young Lord was driven north into exile.)]

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：少帝以中人之才，嗣將墜之業，屬上天不祐，仍歲大饑，尚或絕強敵之歡盟，鄙輔臣之謀略。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The Young Emperor, with the talent of an ordinary man, succeeded to a falling enterprise; Heaven did not aid him, and year after year there was great famine; he still might have severed the friendly alliance with a powerful enemy and despised the stratagems of his assisting ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: The Young Emperor had only ordinary ability yet inherited a dynasty on the verge of collapse. Heaven withheld its favor, famine struck year after year, yet he still broke the alliance with a powerful enemy and scorned the counsel of his ministers.

sentences.zh: 奢淫自縱，謂有泰山之安；

translations.literal: Luxurious and dissolute, he indulged himself, thinking he had the security of Mount Tai;
translations.idiomatic: He gave himself to luxury and dissipation, believing himself as secure as Mount Tai;

sentences.zh: 委托非人，坐受平陽之辱。

translations.literal: he entrusted affairs to unworthy men and sat idle to receive the disgrace of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: he entrusted power to the wrong men and sat idle until he suffered the disgrace of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 族行萬里，身老窮荒。

translations.literal: His clan traveled ten thousand li; he grew old in a desolate wilderness.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was driven ten thousand li; he grew old in a desolate land.

sentences.zh: 自古亡國之醜者，無如帝之甚也。

translations.literal: Among the disgraces of fallen states since antiquity, none has been as extreme as this emperor's.
translations.idiomatic: Among the disgraces of fallen rulers since antiquity, none has equaled his.

sentences.zh: 千載之後，其如恥何，傷哉！

translations.literal: A thousand years hence, what shame can compare—how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: A thousand years from now, what shame can compare? How lamentable!
